title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (2026-10-24 edition)
notes: Text of the 2026-10-24 edition read 2026-11-14 (PDF Last-Modified 2026-10-29, 936 pages); the 2026-04-18 edition was read on 2026-10-18 and rechecked on 2026-10-19. The October edition renumbers the agent section from 4.1.24 (pages 254 to 260 in April) to 4.1.23, Agentic Platform Requirements (pages 263 to 269), with the same rule IDs (ID# 0031167 to 0031177, each marked Last Updated Apr 2026); its summary of changes since the April edition lists no agentic change. One public document holds both rulebooks; the agent rules sit mainly in the Visa Product and Service Rules. 1.1.1.5 (ID# 0007428): the rules govern the relationship between Visa and its Members and their agents and confer no rights on third parties. 1.1.1.3 (ID# 0000385): where the rules conflict with applicable laws or regulations, the laws govern. 4.1.23.2 (ID# 0031168; 4.1.24.2 in April): an Agentic Payment Provider must enroll in and comply with the Visa Intelligent Commerce program and register with Visa, directly or via an Agentic Payment Enabler; obtain a Token from Visa or an Agentic Payment Enabler when it uses a Stored Credential; and not undertake an Agentic Transaction in a Card-Present Environment or aggregate several Agentic Transactions into one. 4.1.23.10 (ID# 0031176; 4.1.24.10 in April): a Cardholder is responsible for any actions an Agentic Payment Provider takes as part of an Agentic Transaction as if the Cardholder initiated the Transaction. Glossary, Cardholder (ID# 0024372): an Agentic Payment Provider is considered the Cardholder for an Agentic Transaction. Glossary, Agentic Payment Provider (ID# 0031164): the provider of an application a Cardholder uses for tasks on the Cardholder's behalf, which can search, discover and purchase on a payment instruction and Cardholder verification, can undertake an Agentic Transaction, can be used at more than one Merchant, stores and transmits a Token (an EMV payment token, ID# 0029108), completes a Transaction by passing the Token to the Merchant, and takes no part in authorization, clearing or settlement. 1.7.6.1 (ID# 0006558): an Issuer must pay the Acquirer for an Agentic Transaction processed in accordance with a Cardholder's payment instructions. 1.7.4.1 (ID# 0029326): an Issuer must not block or decline transactions, including those of Agentic Payment Providers, in a systematic or wholesale manner, with listed exceptions (an immediate fraud threat, law, the rules; a footnote excludes Chile). 5.4.2.5 (ID# 0008771): a Merchant must not require a Cardholder to waive the right to dispute a Transaction, including an Agentic Transaction. 1.5.5.2 (ID# 0006948): a Merchant, Agentic Payment Enabler or Agentic Payment Provider must not surcharge, with regional exceptions. Dispute Condition 10.4, invalid disputes (ID# 0030254): for disputes processed on or after 2026-10-24, the matching data from earlier undisputed transactions includes login IDs for an Agentic Payment Provider. The archived copy (captured 2025-11-24) is the 2025-10-18 edition, which lists these rules under 'Global Agentic Payments/Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) Program Launched', effective 2025-10-18 (2025-11-04 in Chile). Every mention of 'Agentic' in the April 2026 edition was read: Visa calls none of these rules a liability shift, none adds an agent-specific dispute condition, interchange rate or fee, and the text does not mention TAP, 8004, ERC-, x402, ACP, UCP or AP2. In the October 2026 edition 'Trusted Agent' has no hits, 'liability shift' appears only in EMV contexts, and the dispute-evidence rule (Dispute Condition 10.4, in force for disputes processed from 2026-10-24) is unchanged in substance. Visa omits proprietary and security details from the public edition. Rechecked 2026-11-21: the PDF now answers with Last-Modified 2026-11-20, but its XMP creation and modification dates (2026-10-23) and its 936 pages match the 2026-10-24 edition, so the edition is unchanged. A text check the same day found the Summary of Changes still headed as changes since the 18 April 2026 rules, the agent section still 4.1.23 Agentic Platform Requirements, and still no hits for 'Trusted Agent'; the rules were not re-read in full.

title: Visa Intelligent Commerce developer documentation (overview, concepts, workflows and production readiness pages)
notes: Replaced the public VIC overview in October 2026. On 2026-10-19 the rendered overview asked visitors to sign in, and its text and the concepts (/docs/visa-intelligent-commerce/concepts) and workflows (/docs/visa-intelligent-commerce/workflows) pages were read from the page source. On 2026-11-14 the overview, concepts, workflows and production-readiness pages and their .md twins answered HTTP 200 with no sign-in prompt. The overview then said production access requires onboarding to VIC and to the Trusted Agent Protocol, Visa Token Service and Visa Payment Passkeys, plus registration through the Visa Agent Registry Service (VARS) so that Visa can validate agent signatures and merchant encryption keys at credential retrieval. The concepts page said agentSignature is required when the agent is a Trusted Agent Provider or the token requestor is a Wallet Provider and is not sent for an Open Source Agent; instructions default to a 30-day intent expiration in the US; at most 15 cryptograms per token in a rolling 24 hours; the restricted MCC list sits in a VIC and TAP Client Implementation Guide, named without a link; and US merchants that support 3-D Secure receive a Program Not Supported response for agentic transactions in the US only, while other regions keep 3DS with region-specific treatment and SCA in Europe uses Visa Payment Passkeys. The production-readiness page said Visa's CE3.0 program covers agentic transactions. Card enrollment journey (read 2026-10-19): token provisioned through VTS first, then issuer step-up where required and, if applicable, Visa Payment Passkey setup with device binding; credential retrieval only after that unless the use case is approved to skip the passkey. Workflows (read 2026-10-19; the authentication step reads the same on 2026-11-14): the consumer authenticates the instruction through a Visa Payment Passkey or other issuer-approved methods; the agent submits the credential to the merchant checkout or a PSP-enabled flow; Visa retains post-purchase confirmation data for disputes. No fees or pricing were stated on either date. Rechecked 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200): the overview still gives the production onboarding requirements (TAP, VTS, VPP, VARS registration) and states no fees; the concepts .md twin still gives the US 3-D Secure behavior.

title: Visa Merchant Registry Service (VMRS) in the Trusted Agent Protocol API reference
notes: Read 2026-11-14 (HTTP 200) from this .md twin and from the OpenAPI 3.1.0 document embedded in https://developer.visa.com/api-reference/trusted-agent-protocol/get-v1-trustedagentprotocol (info.title Trusted Agent Protocol, version 1, server https://sandbox.api.visa.com). Tag Visa Merchant Registry Service, described as a micro service that manages merchant identities and distributes encryption keys for payment request encryption in the TAP ecosystem; navigation bundle TRAP.102, public. Nine operations: POST /vmrs/v1/merchants (201; 409 when the merchantUrl already exists; 422); GET and PUT /vmrs/v1/merchants/{merchantId}; GET and POST /vmrs/v1/merchants/{merchantId}/keys (new keys are created deactivated); GET, PUT and DELETE /vmrs/v1/merchants/{merchantId}/keys/{keyId}; POST /vmrs/v1/merchants/{merchantId}/keys/{keyId}/activate. 15 schemas. MerchantCreate requires indicator (TAP, ACG or BOTH; described only as the transaction processing type), merchantName and merchantUrl; optional vmid, encryptionKey (KeyCreate), cryptogramType (TAVV or DAVV, default DAVV), apiIntegrations and webIntegrations (url, integrationSpec, metadata), paymentPayloadType (UNENCRYPTED or ENCRYPTED, default UNENCRYPTED), protocolInteractions (protocol ucp, acp or x402, with url, documentationUrl and metadata) and acceptanceRelationships (example visa, mastercard). KeyCreate requires keyName, algorithm (RSA-OAEP, RSA-OAEP-256, RSA-OAEP-384 or RSA-OAEP-512, a key wrapping algorithm), encryptionKey (a Base64-encoded asymmetric public key in DER, PEM, JWK or OpenSSH format) and encryptionType (A256GCM, A128GCM, C20P, A256CBC_HS512, A128CBC_HS256, A256CCM or A128CCM, a content encryption algorithm); expirationDate is optional and must be in the future. A CredentialsResponse schema (vmid, merchantId, merchantName, merchantUrl, encryptionKey, cryptogramType, paymentPayloadType) is referenced by no path. No security scheme is declared. Not in the reference on 2026-10-19 (see src-visa-tap-apiref).

title: MPP identity documentation (extensions/identity, source of mpp.dev/extensions/identity)
notes: Read with git show at origin/main d062df6 (2026-11-14) in research/vendor/mpp; the file last changed in 91a3996 (2026-11-12). Live at https://mpp.dev/extensions/identity (HTTP 200, 2026-11-14), where https://mpp.dev/advanced/identity now redirects. mppx runs each route verifier at most once per request, before it issues a Challenge, so rejected callers never see payment terms; routes without identity skip identity checks, not payment checks. title: Visa Agentic Ready for Acceptance Program
notes: Undated program page, linked from the 2026-11-17 release. Read 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200, 563,730 bytes); the stage cards for each role were read from the content JSON embedded in the page. Four stages: access, discovery and cart, payment, post-purchase. Merchant: access, configure bot management to recognize trusted agent traffic and register and configure merchant endpoints in the Agentic Directory; discovery and cart, agent-discoverable product data, agent-driven cart creation and generative engine optimization; payment, ensure cryptogram submission and enable guest checkout for agent-driven transactions; post-purchase, link transactions to the underlying payment credentials and link those credentials to the underlying card using PAR. PSP or acquirer: access, register and configure merchant endpoints in the Agentic Directory; discovery and cart, no requirements; payment, process tokenized credentials, ensure cryptogram submission, link account verification results to the subsequent authorization, and risk and fraud configuration; post-purchase, the same two links. B2B supplier: access adds an alternate workflow for a verified agent that hits a blocker and agent-enabled login with delegated consumer authorization; payment, identify and process tokenized credentials, cryptogram submission and guest checkout. The framework says trusted agent traffic and never names TAP; the page links Visa's TAP documentation only in a related-content card. FAQ: the program sits within Visa Intelligent Commerce; asked how it relates to ACP, UCP, AP2 or MCP, Visa calls it protocol-agnostic; it says agentic transactions are live with major AI platforms and that PSPs and acquirers are the primary participants. The linked program guide on docs.visa.com asks for sign-in and was not read.
